name: Critical alerts
plain: A notification that rings through Do Not Disturb, Focus and the mute switch.
meaning: For emergencies like glucose alarms. Powerful enough that Apple demands justification.

android.permission: ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY (special) to bypass DND; USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT limited by Play
android.prompt_ui: Do Not Disturb access page in Settings
android.revocation: Settings > Notifications > Do Not Disturb access
android.store_policy: Play: full screen intent restricted to calling and alarm apps (Android 14)
android.note: User must also allow channel to bypass DND

ios.prompt_ui: Separate permission prompt for Critical Alerts
ios.note: Apple request form required; time sensitive notifications (iOS 15) need only a capability

limits.headline: Can ring through Do Not Disturb, Focus and the mute switch, if Apple approves the app
limits.user_action: You tap Allow on a separate Critical Alerts prompt, or give Do Not Disturb access on Android
can: Sound an alert even when Focus or the mute switch is on
Warn you about things like a health reading or emergency
Bypass Do Not Disturb on Android once you grant it
cannot: Do this on iPhone without Apple's special approval for the app
Do this if you decline the Critical Alerts prompt
Bypass Do Not Disturb on Android unless you also allow that channel to
limits.reach_label: Only for the rare urgent alert
limits.differs: iPhone needs a special Apple approval plus its own prompt. Android needs Do Not Disturb access and a channel that is allowed to bypass.

story.what_it_is: An alert that rings through silent mode, Do Not Disturb and Focus.

marketing.name: Critical Alerts
marketing.pitch: Apple lets approved health and safety apps send alerts that sound even when the phone is silenced.

story.for_you: Your phone sounds off at night even on silent because a blood sugar or home alarm app sent a critical alert. You see a separate permission prompt for it.
story.for_makers: Makers of health and safety apps need it for alarms that cannot be missed. Apple asks for a justification, because it is powerful and could be abused.

use_cases.example: A glucose monitor wakes a sleeping person when sugar drops too low.
A home alarm sounds on your phone when a smoke or break in alert fires.
A water leak sensor alerts you at 3 am.
A medical device app warns of a pump or heart rhythm problem.
A hospital paging app alerts a nurse to a code blue.
An emergency alert app warns of a local storm.
A game cannot get this and uses normal alerts, since Apple reserves it for safety.

story.android_note: Android has no exact match. A user can allow a channel to bypass Do Not Disturb.
story.ios_note: iOS requires Apple approval and a separate prompt.

technical_bounds: Apple requires a form and approval
The person can still disable per app

history.change: Critical alerts introduced with Apple entitlement
